## Context / Problem
Merge-abort recovery for the tickets branch is written twice.

`_store/sync.py` (reconverge) owns the whole toolkit: the abort-message parser
(`_merge_abort_named_paths` + `_untracked_overwrite_paths` + `_local_change_paths`),
the quarantine dir arithmetic (`_quarantine_dir_under`), the quarantine MOVER
(`_quarantine_untracked`) and the local-change restore (`_restore_local_changes`)
— roughly `sync.py:221-339`.

`_store/push_recovery.py` re-implements the mover as `_quarantine_untracked_paths`
(`push_recovery.py:236-260`) and reaches sideways into sync for the two pure pieces
(`from rebar._store.sync import _quarantine_dir_under, _untracked_overwrite_paths`,
line 56, under a seven-line comment explaining why the mover could NOT be shared).
The stated reason is real: every git call in `push_recovery` must run through the
late-bound `core._git` seam that ~25 `push._git` monkeypatch sites depend on, while
sync's mover shells through sync's own module-level `_git`.

The two movers have already DRIFTED. `push_recovery._quarantine_untracked_paths`
checks `git status --porcelain -uall` for `??` on every named path before it moves
anything (a mis-parse must never relocate TRACKED data); `sync._quarantine_untracked`
has no such fence, and neither does the third caller,
`_commands/doctor.py::_quarantine_leftovers`, which calls sync's mover directly.
Bugs `small-delicious-loris` (6ccc) and `sulfuryl-suicidal-osprey` (573a) are the
same defect landing in the two paths one at a time — exactly the instalment pattern
the parent epic was opened for.

Prior work has already shared the ADJACENT pieces, and this ticket must not re-do
them: `d6e3-548c-37eb-4c45` made `_store/git_outcome.py` the single failure-marker
table and `gitutil.run_git_bounded` the single synthetic-timeout fold, and both
merges already retry a TRANSIENT_FS fault through the shared
`gitutil._with_transient_fault_retry` / `git_outcome.classify`. What is left is the
merge-abort recovery toolkit above.

## Approach
Add `src/rebar/_store/merge_recovery.py` as the neutral owner, taking the git runner
as a plain callable (`git(path, *args) -> CompletedProcess`) so BOTH the sync
module-level `_git` and the late-bound `core._git` fit without either side losing its
patch point:

- `abort_named_paths` / `untracked_overwrite_paths` / `local_change_paths` and the
  trailer-prefix table — moved verbatim from `sync.py` (pure, no subprocess).
- `quarantine_dir_under` / `quarantine_dir` — moved from `sync.py`.
- `quarantine_untracked(git, tracker, paths)` — ONE mover, unifying the two on
  push_recovery's stricter shape: resolve `--git-common-dir`, verify `??` for every
  named path BEFORE moving any, then `shutil.move` each into the timestamped
  quarantine; any refusal answers `False` with nothing moved.
- `restore_local_changes(git, tracker, paths)` — moved from `sync.py`.

Do NOT fuse the two merge control flows into one `merge_remote()`. They are
genuinely different (sync: union merge, unrelated-histories case, restore-from-HEAD,
warn-and-keep-local; push_recovery: stash-commit set-aside, transport-retry loop,
`_raise_if_strict` reason codes, tri-state return), and a single function
parameterised over those is a worse module than two callers of one toolkit.

`sync.py` keeps `_quarantine_untracked`, `_restore_local_changes`,
`_untracked_overwrite_paths`, `_local_change_paths` and `_quarantine_dir_under` as
thin delegating adapters — the names `doctor.py` and the pinning tests bind, and the
names `sync._recover_merge_abort` resolves at module scope so its monkeypatch keeps
working. `push_recovery` KEEPS `_quarantine_untracked_paths(core, base_path, paths)`
with its exact current signature, also as a thin delegating adapter that resolves
`core._git` at call time — `tests/unit/test_push_recovery_untracked.py` calls it
directly (lines 286, 358, 372) and `monkeypatch.setattr`s the name (line 311), and
`_retry_untracked_overwrite` resolves it at module scope, so the SYMBOL must survive
even though its body does not. `push_recovery`'s `from rebar._store.sync import ...`
line goes away; both adapters' bodies become one call into `merge_recovery`.

## Latent divergence converged (epic AC2)
The `??` fence reaches `sync` and `doctor` for the first time. It is a no-op on every
path that exists today — sync's inputs come from git's own "untracked working tree
files would be overwritten" list, and doctor's come from
`dirty_tracker_classes()["leftovers"]`, which is built from `??` status lines — so no
pinned behaviour changes. A NEW test covers the convergence directly: sync's mover
must refuse, and move nothing, when handed a TRACKED path.

## Guard construction
See the 'Guard construction (moved from description)' comment on this ticket for the full guard spec (moved to fit the 8000-char review admission limit).

## Scope
`src/rebar/_store/merge_recovery.py` (new), `src/rebar/_store/sync.py`,
`src/rebar/_store/push_recovery.py`, `tests/unit/store/test_merge_recovery.py` (new).
`_engine_support/reads.py` and `_commands/doctor.py` are NOT touched — they call
`sync.reconverge` / `sync._quarantine_untracked`, both of which keep their signature.

## Testing
New (`tests/unit/store/test_merge_recovery.py`): the shared mover moves an untracked
leftover into quarantine and answers True; refuses a tracked path and moves nothing;
refuses an unresolvable `--git-common-dir`; refuses a path that vanished; the parser
returns [] when the marker is absent; the uniqueness guard plus its three mutation
cases (unmarked copy fails, reasoned marker passes, bare marker fails).

Pinning, to pass with NO assertion edits: `tests/unit/test_store_sync_reconverge.py`,
`tests/unit/test_sync_union_recovery.py`, `tests/unit/test_push_recovery_untracked.py`,
`tests/unit/test_push_retry_stash_pop.py`, `tests/unit/test_commit_and_push_tickets_branch.py`,
`tests/unit/test_commit_and_push_tickets_branch_heldout.py`,
`tests/unit/test_push_strict.py`, `tests/unit/test_push_strict_happy.py`,
`tests/unit/store/test_git_outcome.py`, `tests/unit/test_doctor_dirty_tree.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Exactly one quarantine mover and one merge-abort parser exist under `src/rebar`;
      checked by `tests/unit/store/test_merge_recovery.py` uniqueness guard passing in
      the default `Verified` tier, and by
      `test -z "$(grep -rl 'shutil\.move\|shutil\.copy2' src/rebar | grep -v merge_recovery.py)"`
      exiting 0.
- [x] `push_recovery.py` no longer imports from `sync.py`, while still exposing
      `_quarantine_untracked_paths`; checked by
      `! grep -q "from rebar._store.sync import" src/rebar/_store/push_recovery.py`
      exiting 0 AND
      `python -c "from rebar._store import push_recovery as p; assert p._quarantine_untracked_paths"`
      exiting 0.
- [x] No pinned behaviour changes: every pinning suite named above passes with no edit
      to any assertion; checked by `git diff origin/main -- <the ten pinning files
      named in Testing>` printing NOTHING (they are untouched; the only tests/ change
      is the new `tests/unit/store/test_merge_recovery.py`), and by
      `pytest <those ten files> -q` reporting 0 failures.
- [x] The net non-test line delta is RECORDED (not gated) on the ticket, per the epic's
      measured finding that extraction costs more in the documented owner than it
      recovers; checked by a `rebar comment` carrying `git show --numstat`.

## Close verification (orphan takeover, 2026-08-22)
Commit 037d4da8373 merged to main (verified at 8a036765705). AC1: shutil.move/copy2 grep clean outside merge_recovery.py, tests/unit/store/test_merge_recovery.py 11/11 pass. AC2: no sync import in push_recovery.py; _quarantine_untracked_paths importable. AC3: pinning suites pass post-merge, no assertion edits (change landed via Gerrit review). AC4: numstat delta recorded in comment. Boxes checked with this evidence.
